entry.title: Gaussian Difference Dynamics: Breaking the $2^{n/2}$ Barrier for the Shortest Vector Problem and Discrete Gaussian Sampling
entry.summary:
We give classical randomized algorithms in a word-RAM model that break the $2^{n/2}$ barrier for both discrete Gaussian sampling (DGS) and the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP). For every fixed $\alpha>1$, shifted DGS on arbitrary lattices at width $\sigma\ge\alpha\eta_{1/2}(L)$ takes $$ (3/2)^{n/2+o(n)}\text{ time} \qquad\text{and}\qquad (4/3)^{n/2+o(n)}\text{ space}. $$ These bounds match the Becker--Ducas--Gama--Laarhoven (BDGL) heuristic sieving exponents.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Averaging Collusion Breaks Traceability in Personalized Neural Audio Watermarking
entry.summary:
Personalized neural audio watermarking systems embed user-specific payloads into audio to trace the user associated with a leaked or misused copy. Existing evaluations mainly assume access to a single personalized copy, but real-world distribution may expose multiple copies of the same recording. We find that simple sample-wise averaging breaks traceability: averaging only two copies produces tracing-failure rates of 87.7-99.7% across the five systems while largely preserving audio quality.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #multimodal #neuroscience

entry.title: Hidden Curves and Short Duals: Cubic Jets, Dual Leaks, and the Limits of Masked-Code Encryption
entry.summary:
Masked-code encryption hides a decodable code behind a transformation meant to make it look random. We study the two masks proposed as compact alternatives to Goppa codes---Wang's RLCE and the $(U\,|\,U{+}V)$ construction of UVW-KEM---over the decodable hidden codes they have been or could be applied to, and find that, among the families examined, none yields a compact trapdoor. Over Reed--Solomon and algebraic-geometry codes the mask hides a \emph{curve}, and curves are not hidden from jets.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Provenance Proofs: Linkable Zero-Knowledge Derivation Relations for Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets
entry.summary:
ZKPoSP proves that a public key or address was honestly derived from a hidden wallet seed, without revealing the seed or the private derivation state. This paper studies relationships among several derived values: whether public keys or addresses, possibly on different curves and different blockchains, share a hidden origin, which is the seed or an anchor of the wallet, and who else can recognize this relation. We give a model for such provenance proofs, with derivation proofs, which carry a link value, and provenance proofs, which show that several derivation statements share an origin.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: (R)Icy-DVRF: A Robust Distributed Verifiable Random Function Based on ROAST Signatures
entry.summary:
Ensuring robustness and liveness in distributed verifiable random functions (DVRFs) allows the protocol to maintain correct operation and guarantee output generation, even in the presence of malicious actors attempting to disrupt the process, delay cryptographic shares, or remain unresponsive. Because existing DVRF protocols typically rely on synchronous or semi-synchronous network assumptions, simultaneously achieving these properties remains a challenge. To address this limitation, this paper enhances the FROST-based Icy-DVRF protocol to achieve both robustness and liveness.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: A proof of P≠NP (New symmetric encryption algorithm against any linear attacks and differential attacks)
entry.summary:
P vs NP problem is the most important unresolved problem in the field of computational complexity. Its impact has penetrated into all aspects of algorithm design, especially in the field of cryptography. The security of cryptographic algorithms based on short keys depends on whether P is equal to NP.
